title: Ideal Low-Degree Junta Hypothesis
statement: Let $n,k$ be nonnegative integers, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function, let $P\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and fix an assignment of signs to the coordinates in $P$. Let $\delta\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $0<\delta\le 1/2$, and choose an input batch indexed by the restricted sample count, with each entry an assignment of signs to the coordinates outside $P$. The low-degree $\mathbb{F}_2$ learner applied to the batch labeled by the restriction of $f$ equals the learner applied to the corresponding reindexed inputs labeled by that same restricted function, where the learner's degree bound is $k-\lfloor 3k/4\rfloor$ and its sample count is the prescribed polynomial sample count.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on $n$ signs
$P$ is a subset of the $n$ coordinates
input batch indexed by the restricted sample count, with entries assignments on coordinates outside $P$
